title: Global rate limiter: exact or fast?
brief: Design a rate limiter for an API served from 3 regions. Every request checks a counter before it's served. Use three Region blocks (us, eu, ap), each holding its own client and edge service: calls that cross a region add 70 ms. Use a Cache block as the counter store (Redis INCR with a TTL).

requirements: 6k rps, split evenly across the 3 regions (90% checks, 10% config writes)
A customer's limit must be exact across regions: billing depends on it
variants.twist: The eu region is cut off: partition_region('eu'). Your counter is on the other side. Fail open (let traffic through) or fail closed (reject)? Which one would a payments API pick, and which a CDN?

requirements: Limits may overshoot a little: each region counts on its own and syncs in the background
variants.twist: A customer spreads a burst across all 3 regions to get 3x their limit. How far can they overshoot, and how would you bound it (split the limit per region, sync more often)?

hints: Where does the counter live, and how far is it from each edge?
One central counter is exact, but two of three regions pay a cross-region round trip on every request. A counter in each region is fast, but each one sees only its own traffic.

Exact: every region has to check the same counter. Where does it live, and what does that cost the far regions in latency? Fast: each region checks its own counter. What do you give up in accuracy, and how would the counters catch up with each other?
_notes: Each region: client -> edge service. 2k rps per region. Central counter (one cache in us): eu and ap pay 70 ms. Edge 3 replicas: p99 ~96 ms, $1.05; more replicas don't remove the 70 ms. Local counters (a cache per region): edge 3: p99 ~26 ms, $1.35 (over exact's $1.20). So exact forces central (it's cheapest), fast forces local (latency). Exactness isn't simulated: a local design under 'exact' only fails on cost. Ask why it's wrong anyway. Token bucket vs sliding window is worth a minute. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
